o: Urban cooperative banks (UCBs) are mostly engaged in retail banking.
Most of them are permitted to deal in foreign exchange directly.
Their exposure to non-fund business is limited.
Their lending is primarily to MSMEs and individuals (retail loans) in non-rural locations.
w: B is incorrect: most UCBs are NOT permitted to deal in foreign exchange directly.

s:
Which among the following is feature of FinTech?
1. Online Search Engine
2. Financial Services
3. Peer-to-peer Lending
w: Fintech = financial services delivered through technology, e.g., P2P lending. An online search engine is not fintech.

s: Which among the following statement is incorrect with respect to National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID)?
o: The NaBFID has only developmental objectives.
NaBFID does not take deposits from the general public.
The government initially holds 100% of the shares in the bank, which may subsequently be reduced to 26%
The NaBFID was set up as a corporate body with an authorised share capital of Rs. 1 lakh crore
w: A is incorrect — NaBFID has BOTH developmental and financial objectives. It doesn't take public deposits; the Government initially held 100% (minimum 26% later); authorised capital ₹1 lakh crore.

s: The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFlD) was set up as a corporate body with an authorised share capital of______.
w: NaBFID's authorised share capital is ₹1 lakh crore.

s:
Which among the following is the business that RBI cannot Transact as per the RBI Act, 1934?
1. Engage in trade or otherwise have a direct interest in any commercial, industrial, or other undertaking
2. Purchase the shares of any banking company or of any other company, or grant loans upon the security of any such shares
4. Make loans or advances
w: Sec 19 RBI Act bars RBI from trading or holding direct interests in undertakings, buying shares of banks/companies or lending against them, and making unsecured loans or advances. Keyed: all.

s: Which among the following is the provisions mentioned in Section 24 of Banking Regulation Act, 1949?
w: Sec 24 BR Act deals with SLR.

s:
Which among the following is/are the reasons for establishing Development Financial Institutions (DFI)?
1. Commercial banks’ ability to lend for longer periods, as required for infrastructure projects in developing economies, is limited.
2. Development Financial Institutions (DFIs) play significant role in provision of long-term credit contributing to capital formation for sustained growth.
3. Commercial banks mobilise short-term resources in the form of customer deposits.
w: All three are reasons: banks can't lend long, DFIs provide long-term credit for capital formation, and banks' resources are short-term deposits.

s: Which among the following was the first Development Financial Institution (DFI) established in India?
o: National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID)
National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development (NABARD)
w: IFCI, set up in 1948, was the first DFI.

s: Which among the following provides refinance to banks for industrial purposes?
w: ICICI, IDBI and NABARD all provided refinance (keyed: all).

s: ______ was the first Development Financial Institution (DFI) to be listed in New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).
o: Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI)
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
w: ICICI was the first Indian company (and first DFI) listed on the NYSE (1999).

s: Which among the following has the maximum tenure of Direct Loan provided by SIDBI to MSMEs?
o: SIDBI Make in India Soft Loan Fund for MSMEs (SMILE)
Loans under partnership with OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer)
SIDBI - Loan for Purchase of Equipment for Enterprise's Development (SPEED)
w: SIDBI SMILE loans can run up to 10 years, the longest among these.

s:
Which among the following statement(s) is/are correct with respect to Self-Help Groups (SHGs)?
1. These are small informal groups of 10-20 individuals, who are homogenous with respect to social and economic background.
2. The main aim is to promote savings habit among members and to raise and manage resources, for benefit of group members.
3. It is preferred that all the members are from Above poverty Line level (APL).
w: SHGs are informal groups of 10–20 homogeneous members that promote savings. Members are generally BPL/poor, not APL, so 3 is wrong.

s: Which among the following Micro Finance Institutions which are for profit?
w: NBFC-MFIs are for-profit MFIs. Societies/trusts are not-for-profit; mutual-benefit MFIs are co-operatives.

s:
NBFCs are not eligible for Bank Credit for which among the following activities?
1. All Bills discounted/rediscounted by NBFCs.
2. Investments of NBFCs both of current and long-term nature.
3. Unsecured loans/inter corporate deposits by NBFCs to/in any company.
4. Finance to NBFCs for further lending to individuals for subscribing to Initial Public Offerings (IPOs).
w: Banks may not finance NBFCs for bill discounting/rediscounting, investments, unsecured loans/ICDs to companies, or on-lending for IPO subscription — all four.

s:
Which among the following is/are the benefit(s) of the Niryat Bandhu Scheme?
1. The overall goal of the DGFT Niryat Bandhu Scheme is to use international commerce and e- commerce exports as a catalyst for economic development
2. It aims to support exporters to accelerate India's export growth trajectory.
3. The objective of the Niryat Bandhu Scheme is to reach out to the new and potential exporters and mentor them through orientation programmes, counselling sessions
w: Niryat Bandhu (DGFT) uses trade/e-commerce exports as a catalyst for development, supports export growth and mentors new exporters — all three.

s: ______ is the sole national reinsurer in India which provides reinsurance to insurers in India as well as abroad.
w: GIC Re is the national reinsurer. Foreign reinsurers also operate through branches in GIFT City/India.

s:
Which among the following is/are the Insurance Depositories licensed presently by IRDAI?
1. NSDL Database Management Ltd
2. Central Insurance Repository Ltd
3. SHCIL Projects Ltd
4. Karvy Insurance Repository Ltd
w: IRDAI-licensed insurance repositories include NSDL Database Management, Central Insurance Repository (CDSL), SHCIL Projects and Karvy (KFin) — all four.

s:
Which among the following is/are the feature(s) of E-Insurance Account?
1. Each e-Insurance Account has a unique account number and each account holder is granted a Login ID and Password, to access their e-policies.
2. e-Insurance Account is offered free of cost to the applicants.
3. An individual who does not have an insurance policy, cannot open an e-Insurance Account.
w: An e-insurance account has a unique number with login and is free. A person can open one even without an existing policy, so 3 is wrong.

s:
Which among the following statement(s) best describes the role of RBI in India?
1. It is the Monetary Authority in India which takes care of formulation of Monetary Policy.
2. The Reserve Bank of India is the nation's sole note issuing authority.
3. All banks maintain accounts with RBI to facilitate transfer of funds and settle inter-bank transactions.
w: RBI is the monetary authority, sole note-issuer (except ₹1 notes/coins, issued by the Government) and banker to banks — all three as keyed.

s: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has ______ number of whole-time members?
w: IRDAI has 5 whole-time members (plus a Chairperson and 4 part-time members).

s:
Which among the following is/are the channels through which the funds reach the infrastructure sector in India?
1. Government
2. Development Financial Institutions
3. Commercial Banks
4. Non-Banking Financial Companies
5. Insurance Companies & Pension Funds
w: Infrastructure is funded by government, DFIs, commercial banks, NBFCs (incl. IFCs), and insurance & pension funds — all five.

s: Which among the following is the number of Independent Directors of National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID)?
w: The NaBFID board includes a few (not a fixed number of) independent directors as keyed in the book.

s: The concept of the Bad Bank in India is to have National Asset Reconstruction Company (NARCL) coupled with a debt resolution company (i.e.) ______.
o: National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID)
Asset Management Company of India Ltd.
w: The bad-bank structure pairs NARCL (asset aggregator) with India Debt Resolution Company Ltd (IDRCL, the asset manager).

s:
Which among the following is/are the benefit(s) of establishing National Asset Reconstruction Company (NARCL)?
1. Take over NPAs from banks.
2. Free up the balance sheets of the bank and enable them to concentrate on business development.
3. To aggregate and consolidate stressed assets for their subsequent resolution.
w: NARCL takes over NPAs, frees bank balance sheets and consolidates stressed assets for resolution — all three.

s: It is expected that sale of the bad loans to National Asset Reconstruction Company (NARCL) will be against ______ cash and balance ______ being in the form of Security Receipts (SRs).
w: NARCL pays 15% in cash and 85% as security receipts.

s: Which among the following is the maximum tenure for Notice money available for banks?
w: Notice money maximum tenure is 14 days.

s: Which among the following is not a tenure of Treasury Bill issued in India?
w: 274-day is not a T-Bill tenor.

s: In which among the following financing processes Double Discounting takes place?
w: Double discounting happens in bill rediscounting — the bank discounts the bill, then rediscounts it with another institution.

s: Which among the following can be called as Auction market?
w: Stock exchanges are auction (order-driven) markets where buyers and sellers bid against each other.

s: Which among the following is the regulator of Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE)?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)
w: SEBI regulates stock exchanges including BSE.

s: Which among the following was the first Stock Exchange in GIFT City, Gujarat?
o: National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. (NSE)
w: India INX (BSE's subsidiary, Jan 2017) was the first international exchange in GIFT City.

s:
Which among the following is/are the promoters of National Securities Depository Ltd (NSDL)?
1. Industrial Development Bank of India
2. Unit Trust of India
3. Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE)
w: NSDL was promoted by IDBI, UTI and NSE — not BSE.

s:
Which among the following statement(s) is/are correct with respect to Red Herring Prospectus (RHP)?
1. It is a prospectus which has all the details with respect to an issue of a Company.
2. In case of book building process, the price of issued securities is mentioned
w: An RHP lacks complete details of price and quantity, so 1 is wrong; it does not mention the final price under book building, so 2 is wrong. Neither.

s:
Which among the following entities can purchase Government Securities in India?
1. Banks
2. Primary Dealers
3. Companies
w: Banks, PDs, companies, individuals and others can all buy G-secs.

s:
Which among the following is/are eligible Participants in the Negotiated Dealing System Order Matching (NDS-OM) platform?
1. Banks
2. Primary dealers
3. Insurance companies
w: NDS-OM participants include banks, PDs, insurance companies, MFs and others (retail via RDS/brokers).

s:
Which among the following is/are instruments traded over the Negotiated Dealing System Order Matching (NDS-OM)?
1. Government Securities
2. T-Bills
3. State Development Loans (SDLs)
4. Corporate Bonds
w: NDS-OM trades G-secs, T-Bills and SDLs. Corporate bonds trade on exchange RFQ platforms.

s: Consider two bonds, Bond B1 has a coupon rate of 9% while Bond B2 has a coupon rate 10% and both have a maturity period of 5 years. Which among them is more sensitive?
o: Both B1 and B2 have same sensitivity
Cannot be determined using the given information.
w: With the same maturity, the LOWER-coupon bond (9%, B1) is more price-sensitive.

s:
Which among the following statement(s) is/are correct with respect to Primary Dealers?
1. Primary dealers are entities, registered with SEBI, who have the license to purchase and sell government securities.
2. Primary Dealers create a market for government securities.
3. RBI guidelines stipulate that PDs should have a minimum turnover ratio
w: PDs are registered with RBI, not SEBI. They make markets in G-secs and must meet a minimum turnover ratio. So 2 and 3.

s:
Which among the following statement(s) is/are correct with respect to the RBI Retail Direct Scheme (RDS)?
1. The scheme provides the facilities to retail investors in government securities market to open and maintain a 'Retail Direct Gilt Account'(RDG Account)
2. The scheme enables corporates to buy and sell Government of India Treasury Bills.
3. Non-Resident retail investors eligible to invest in Government Securities under Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, are eligible under the scheme.
w: RDS gives retail investors an RDG account, and eligible NRIs may join. Corporates are NOT eligible, so 2 is wrong.

s:
Which among the following is/are the characteristics of Forex markets?
1. The market operates the enormous money supply and gives absolute freedom in opening or closing a position in the current market quotation.
2. With a 24-hour work schedule, participants in the forex market need not wait to any given event
3. The forex market has traditionally no service charges, except for the natural bid/ask market spread between the supply and the demand price.
w: All three are standard forex-market features: huge liquidity, 24-hour trading, and costs mainly in the bid-ask spread.

s: Which among the following is the Alternative Reference Rate (ARR) suggested by the UK?
w: The UK's ARR is SONIA.

s: SARON is the Alternate reference Rate suggested by ______.
w: SARON is Switzerland's ARR.

s:
Which among the following is/are the FEDAI members?
1. Public sector banks
2. Private sector banks
3. Co-operative banks
w: FEDAI members are authorised dealers — public, private, foreign and co-operative banks.

s: Which among the following is not a feature of FX Retail Platform?
o: This Platform is available to any customer of a bank
Ceiling on number of transactions per customer during a day
Required to register on CCIL platform
Customers can choose to convert his foreign exchange requirement through any bank of his choice
w: FX Retail has no ceiling on the number of transactions per day. Any bank customer can register with CCIL through their bank and choose any bank.

s: Which among the following is the component which forms the largest component of U.S. Dollar Index (USDX)?
w: The euro has the largest weight in the US Dollar Index (~57.6%).
r: USDX: EUR, JPY, GBP, CAD, SEK, CHF.

s: What is interconnectedness?
o: Countries of the world are connected to one another and the ups and downs in one part of the globe can have a resonating effect, on other parts of the globe.
The rise in prices of commodities brings about a drop in demand of commodities
Components of World Trade Organisation’s measures to improve trade
w: Interconnectedness means world economies are linked, so shocks in one part ripple across the globe.

s: Which among the following is the core principle of working of Merchant Banks?
o: They help individuals in investing in REITs and InvITs
They help corporates and High Net-worth Individuals to issue securities.
They help in improving the quality of products of MSMEs
They advice Governments and exporters all over the world to improve global trade
w: The core of merchant banking is helping companies (and HNIs) raise capital by issuing securities.

s: Merchant Banks are regulated by ______.
w: Merchant bankers are registered with and regulated by SEBI (Merchant Bankers Regulations, 1992).

s:
As per SEBI, Category I Merchant Bankers can act as which among the following in India, with respect to an issue of securities?
1. Advisor
2. Consultant
3. Co-manager
4. Underwriter
5. Portfolio manager
6. Issue manager
w: A Category I merchant banker may act as issue manager, adviser, consultant, co-manager, underwriter and portfolio manager — all six.
r: Cat I = everything incl. issue manager.

s:
A Merchant Bank provides which among the following facilities?
1. Raising equity finance
2. Raising debt related finance
w: As per the IIBF book, merchant banks primarily help raise equity and equity-related finance (commercial banks do debt finance).

s: In terms of SEBI guidelines with respect to Merchant Banks, all debenture issues (public rights) of the companies with the maturity period exceeding ______are required to have "Debenture Trustee".
w: Debenture issues with maturity over 18 months must appoint a debenture trustee.

s: In terms of SEBI guidelines with respect to Merchant Banks, the Company issuing the shares to public shall make arrangements for the use of proceeds of the issue to be monitored by one of the financial institutions, in case of issues, which exceed ______.
w: For public issues above ₹500 crore, use of proceeds must be monitored by a financial institution (monitoring agency), as keyed in the book.

s: A ______ is a contract which gives the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell specified quantity of the underlying assets, at a specific (strike) price, on or before, a specified time (expiration date).
w: An option gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call) or sell (put) at the strike price on/before expiry.

s: Which among the following is the Option which can be exercised by the buyer on or before the expiration date at anytime between the day of purchase of the option and the day of its expiry?
w: An AMERICAN option can be exercised at any time up to expiry; a European option only on the expiry date. (Publisher key 'European' is wrong.)
note: Key corrected — publisher key C corrected to A — American option

s:
Which among the following is/are eligible participants under Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS)?
1. MSME sellers
2. Corporate buyers
3. Government Departments
4. Bank financiers
w: TReDS participants: MSME sellers, corporate/PSU/government buyers and financiers (banks, NBFC-factors) — all four.

s: Uploading invoice in the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) is a process of ______.
w: An MSME seller uploading its invoice on TReDS for financing is factoring. (Buyer-initiated uploads are reverse factoring.)

s:
Venture Capital cannot be provided to entities in India for which among the following activities?
1. Small businesses
2. Real estate
3. Non-banking financial services
4. Gold financing
w: SEBI rules bar VC funds from investing in real estate, NBFC activities and gold financing. Small businesses are core VC targets.

s: With regard to SEBI guidelines for Venture Capital Investments in India, each scheme launched or fund set up by a venture capital fund shall have firm commitment from the investors to contribute at least______, before the start of its operations.
w: Each VCF scheme needed a firm investor commitment of at least ₹5 crore before starting operations (SEBI VCF Regulations).

s:
Which among the following is/are the feature(s) of Operating Leasing?
1. It is mostly used to acquire assets on a relatively short-period basis.
2. The lessor will recover the cost of the asset from multiple lessees.
3. They are typically for assets like computers and windmills.
w: Operating leases are short-term, the lessor recovers cost from several lessees, and they suit assets like computers and windmills — all three.

s: A ______is an arrangement, where the lessor borrows a portion of the purchase price, from some lender/financial institutions.
w: In a leveraged lease the lessor borrows part of the purchase price from a lender.

s: Hire Purchase is ______.
w: Hire purchase is a contract of bailment with an option to purchase.

s: Which among the following is the correct range of CIBIL Score in India?
w: The CIBIL score ranges from 300 to 900.

s: Based on the recommendations contained in the ______Report, RBI issued guidelines to the effect that all Credit Institutions should become members of all Credit Information Companies (CICs).
w: The Aditya Puri Committee recommended that every credit institution become a member of all CICs.

s: No CIC should charge membership fee and annual renewal fees exceeding ______ and ______, respectively.
w: CIC fees are capped at ₹10,000 (membership) and ₹5,000 (annual renewal).

s: The Mutual Funds which have fixed maturity date is ______.
w: Close-ended funds have a fixed maturity date.

s: Mutual Funds are regulated by ______ in India.
w: Mutual funds are regulated by SEBI (MF Regulations, 1996).

s: The Prime Minister Suraksha Bima yojana (PMSBY) is available to people in the age group______.
w: PMSBY is for ages 18–70.

s: The concept of Bancassurance has roots in ______and has spread across different parts of the world since then.
w: Bancassurance originated in France.

s:
In which among the following cases the Insurance Ombudsman cannot take up case?
1. The complainant has made a representation to the concerned insurance company and the insurer has accepted
2. The complaint is made later than one year after the insurer had replied
3. The same complaint is pending in a court.
w: The Insurance Ombudsman cannot take up a complaint after one year of the insurer's reply, or if the matter is pending in court/arbitration. Keyed: all three.

s: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) is regulated by ______.
o: Ministry of Labour, Government of India
Securities and Exchanges Board of India
Pension Funds Regulatory and Development Authority
w: EPFO works under the Ministry of Labour & Employment.

s: The lock-in period is ______for a Public Provident Fund (PPF).
w: PPF lock-in is 15 years.

s: The National Pension Scheme (NPS) is administered and regulated by ______.
o: Securities and Exchanges Board of India
Pension Funds Regulatory and Development Authority
w: NPS is regulated and administered by PFRDA.

s: The number of digits in Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) are ______.
w: PRAN (NPS) is a 12-digit number.

s: Which among the not a type of Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)?
o: Energy such as power generation and distribution
Transport & Logistics, such as roads and highways
Communications, such as optical fibre networks and telecom towers
w: InvITs hold infrastructure assets in energy, transport/logistics and communications — all are types, so 'None of the above'.

s: Which among the following is an example of activity of Quinary Sector?
w: Corporate decision-making by top executives is a quinary activity. Knowledge centres are quaternary; health is tertiary.

s: In a broader sense, Quaternary sector is a sub-sector of______
w: The quaternary (knowledge) sector is a sub-sector of the tertiary sector.

s: Which among the following is not a method of Deficit Financing in India?
o: Borrowing from Public and Foreign Governments
Borrowing from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
Withdrawing Cash Balances held with the Reserve Bank of India
w: Deficit financing = government borrowing from the public/foreign governments, borrowing from RBI, or drawing down its cash balances with RBI. Direct borrowing from the private sector is not listed as a method.

s: Which among the following is the correct Overall Priority Sector Lending target of Small Finance Banks?
w: SFB overall PSL target is now 60% of ANBC/CEOBE (RBI, June 2025; earlier 75%).
note: Adapted PYQ — options updated: SFB target cut to 60%

s: The Bharatmala Pariyojana of the Government of India has been launched to develop ______.
w: Bharatmala Pariyojana develops roads (national highways and corridors).

s:
Which of the following is correct regarding Government of India’s initiatives to boost communication infrastructure in India?
1. National Optical Fibre Network for connectivity to Metros & Urban Areas
2. PLI schemes for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing
3. Tarang Scheme
4. Increase the FDI ceiling on Telecom Sector
w: PLI for electronics, the Tarang Sanchar portal and the raised FDI ceiling in telecom (100% automatic) boost communication infrastructure. The National Optical Fibre Network (BharatNet) targets RURAL gram panchayats, not metros, so 1 is wrong.

s: Which of the following is the National Plan for Multi-Modal Connectivity launched in 2022-23?
w: PM Gati Shakti is the National Master Plan for multi-modal connectivity.

s:
Which of the following is not a form of protectionism?
1. Custom Duty on export of Basmati Rice
2. Tax barrier
3. Non-tax barriers
4. Import Quotas
w: Tax barriers, non-tax barriers and import quotas are forms of protectionism, so 2, 3 and 4 is the keyed answer. A customs duty on EXPORTS of basmati restricts outflow rather than protecting against imports.

s: Which of the following represents LPG era?
w: The book dates the Liberalisation-Privatisation-Globalisation (LPG) era to 1992–2008.

s: Which among the following were not one of the reforms taken up by the Indian Government after 1991?
w: After 1991 India took up strengthening supervision, banking sector reforms and financial sector reforms — all were reforms, so 'None of the above'.

s: Which among the following is correct with respect to Economic Development?
o: It refers to reduction in poverty & unemployment
It is single dimensional in nature
GDP, GNI & PCI are the indicators of Economic Development
w: Economic development refers to reduction in poverty, unemployment and inequality along with growth. A and D describe growth; development is multi-dimensional, not single-dimensional.

s: Which among the following is the type of FDI which is a sort of investment in which, a parent corporation establishes a subsidiary in the destination country and builds operations from scratch?
w: Setting up a subsidiary and building operations from scratch is greenfield FDI.

s:
Match the indicator with what it measures:
A. Savings / Gross Fixed Capital Formation
B. Gross Fixed Capital Formation / GDP
C. GDP growth rate
D. Operating surplus / GVA

i. Performance of the economy
ii. Income share of capital in GDP
iii. Domestic funding of investment
iv. Share of investment in capital goods in GDP
w: Savings/GFCF = domestic funding of investment; GFCF/GDP = share of investment in capital goods; GDP growth = performance of the economy; Operating surplus/GVA = income share of capital.

s:
Which among the following is/are the function(s) of Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA)?
1. Encouraging foreign direct investment into developing countries
2. Protecting investors against non-commercial and political risk
3. Advising governments on how to attract investment
4. Sanctioning long-term infrastructure loans
w: MIGA encourages FDI into developing countries, insures investors against political/non-commercial risk and advises governments. It does NOT lend — that is IBRD/IDA.

s:
India has signed which among the following accords with the World Trade Organisation (WTO)?
1. Reduction of Tariff and Non-Tariff Barriers
2. Trade-Related Investment Measures (TRIMS)
3. Trade-Related Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS)
4. Agreement on Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures (SPM)
5. Multi-Fibre Agreement (MFA)
w: India is party to all of these WTO agreements, including tariff reduction, TRIMS, TRIPS, SPS and the (now phased-out) Multi-Fibre Agreement.

s: Which among the following organisation of World Bank provides soft loans to poorest of the poor countries?
o: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)
w: IDA gives soft (concessional) loans and grants to the poorest countries. IBRD lends to middle-income countries; IFC to the private sector.

s: Which among the following is not one of the functions of the World Trade Organisation (WTO)?
o: Technical assistance and training for developing countries
w: Guaranteeing international loans is MIGA's role, not the WTO's. The WTO handles disputes, monitors trade policies and gives technical assistance.

s: Quantity demanded tends to fall as price rises for two reasons. Which among the following are the two reasons for the same?
w: Quantity demanded falls when price rises because of the substitution effect and the income effect.

s: When prices of a commodity are raised, buyers tend to buy less due to concept of______
w: Buyers buying less at higher prices is the Law of Demand.

s: Which among the following statement is not correct with respect to inflation?
o: Cost-Push Inflation is a type of inflation caused by substantial increases in the cost of production of important goods or services where suitable alternatives are available.
Demand-Pull Inflation is a rise in general prices caused by increasing aggregate demand for goods and services

Increasing quantity of money in the hands of the people increases the aggregate demand for goods and services, and if aggregate supply does not follow suit, prices rise which is called demand-pull inflation.
The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) reflects the change in the level of prices of a basket of goods, at the wholesale level.
w: Statement A is incorrect: cost-push inflation arises when production costs of important goods rise where NO suitable alternatives are available.

s: The frequency with which one unit of currency is used on domestically produced Goods & services in a specific time period is called______
w: The number of times a unit of currency is used to buy domestically produced goods and services in a period is the velocity of money.

s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of Business Cycle?
w: Business cycles are recurring, wave-like, synchronic and PERVASIVE (they affect all sectors). 'Non-pervasive' is not a feature.

s: In which among the following phase(s) of a Business Cycle, once economy reaches the peak, a downward tendency in demand is observed. Also, inflation remains low or shows further signs of falling?
w: After the peak, demand turns down and inflation stays low or falls — the recession phase.

s:
In which phases of Business Cycle, the following characteristics are observed?
1. An extremely low aggregate demand in the economy causes activity to slow down
2. Inflation is comparatively lower
3. Employment avenues begin to close, forcing the unemployment rate to rise rapidly
w: Very low demand, low inflation and rapidly rising unemployment describe the depression phase.

s: The provisions related to the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) to be maintained by banks has been mentioned in which among the following Act?
w: SLR provisions are in the Banking Regulation Act (Sec 24).

s: Which among the following are the lower and upper bands of the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)?
o: Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) and Bank Rate
Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) and Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)
Reverse Repo Rate (RRR) and Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)
Reverse Repo Rate (RRR) and Bank Rate
w: The LAF corridor runs from the SDF (floor) to the MSF (ceiling), with repo in the middle.

s: As per the Reserve Bank of India, a Scheduled Commercial Bank is required to maintain reserves in cash or in the form of Gold or approved securities not exceeding ______ per cent of the total of its demand and time liabilities in India as on the last Friday of the second preceding fortnight.
w: Under Sec 24 BR Act, SLR assets may be prescribed up to a maximum of 40% of NDTL.

s: Banks are not required to publish the internal benchmark/ MCLR for which of the following maturities?
w: Banks publish MCLR for overnight, 1-month, 3-month, 6-month and 1-year tenors (and longer if they choose). There is no 2-month MCLR.

s: Which of the following is not one of the benchmarks suggested by RBI for considering External Benchmark Lending Rates w.e.f. 1st October 2019?
o: GOI 3-months Treasury Bill Yield published by FBIL
GOI 6-months Treasury Bill Yield published by FBIL
w: Permitted external benchmarks (from 1 Oct 2019): RBI repo rate, FBIL 3-month T-bill yield, FBIL 6-month T-bill yield, or any other FBIL benchmark. The reverse repo is not one.

s: Which among the following is the purpose of Reverse Repo Rate?
o: Absorb excess liquidity present with the banks
w: The reverse repo is used to absorb excess liquidity from banks.

s: Which of the following regarding SDF & Reserve Repo is correct?
o: In case of SDF, RBI provides SLR securities as collaterals.
In case of Reverse Repo Rate, RBI provides SLR securities but the same are not counted for SLR maintenance purpose
In case of SDF, no SLR collaterals are provided to banks, however the balance under SDF is eligible for SLR maintenance
w: Under SDF (April 2022) RBI absorbs liquidity without giving collateral, and SDF balances are eligible for SLR. Under reverse repo RBI gives G-sec collateral.
r: SDF = no collateral; floor of the corridor.

s: Which among the following is not one of the limitations of the role of the bank rate as an instrument of monetary policy?
o: The structure of interest rates is not automatically linked to the bank rate
Commercial banks enjoy specific refinance facilities, and may not necessarily rediscount their eligible securities with RBI, at bank rate
The bill market is under-developed and the different sub-markets of the money market are not influenced by the bank rate.
Frequent changes in Bank Rate by RBI bring about uncertainty which effects its applicability
w: A, B and C are textbook limitations of the bank rate. D is not listed among them.

s: Which among the following statement about Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is incorrect?
o: There could be regional disparity in GDP
GDP is an 'aggregate' measure which speaks about how the GDP is distributed among the population of the country.
GDP at market prices measures the value of output at market prices after adjusting for the effect of indirect taxes and subsidies on the prices.
GDP at factor cost, measures the value of output in terms of the price of factors used in its production.
w: B is incorrect: GDP is an aggregate measure and says nothing about how output is DISTRIBUTED among the population.

s: Which among the following is not one of the components of calculation of GDP by Income Approach?
o: Production taxes and depreciation on capital
w: Income approach = compensation of employees + operating surplus (property income) + mixed income + production taxes/depreciation adjustments. Government consumption is an expenditure-side item.

s: Which of the following is the formula for GVA at Basic Price?
o: GVA at Basic Price = GVA at Factor Cost + Production Taxes + Subsidies
GVA at Basic Price = GVA at Factor Cost + Production Taxes - Subsidies
GVA at Basic Price = GVA at Factor Cost - Production Taxes + Subsidies
GVA at Basic Price = GVA at Factor Cost - Production Taxes - Subsidies
w: GVA at basic prices = GVA at factor cost + production taxes − production subsidies.

s: Which among the following is the correct formula for the calculation of Net Domestic Product (NDP) at Factor Cost (FC)?
o: NDP at FC = GDP at MP - Indirect taxes + Subsidies
NDP at FC = GDP at MP + Indirect taxes - Subsidies
NDP at FC = NDP at MP - Indirect taxes + Subsidies
NDP at FC = GNP at MP + Indirect taxes - Subsidies
w: NDP at FC = NDP at MP − indirect taxes + subsidies.

s: ______is the Revenue deficit minus Grants in Aid for creation of capital assets
w: Effective revenue deficit = revenue deficit − grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets.

s: Which among the following is not one of the components of Non-Tax Revenue of the Indian Government?
w: Customs duty is a TAX revenue. Interest receipts, dividends/profits and external grants are non-tax revenue.

s: Which of the following is not a Tax Revenue of Central Government?
w: GST compensation cess is collected for and passed to the GST Compensation Fund for states, so it is not part of the Centre's own tax revenue (as keyed).

s: Which among the following is the best definition of Primary Deficit?
o: It is the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
It is the excess of capital expenditure over capital receipts.
It is the Revenue deficit minus Grants in Aid for creation of capital assets
It is the difference between the fiscal deficit and interest payments.
w: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit minus interest payments.

s: Which among the following is not a regulatory body in India?
w: RBI, SEBI and IRDAI (and PFRDA, IBBI) are financial-sector regulators. RERA regulates real estate, not the financial system.

s: Which among the following is not a financial institution in India?
w: As keyed, chit funds are treated as informal/miscellaneous, not a formal financial institution like NBFCs, pension funds and mutual funds.

s: Which among the following Committees has recommended the establishment of Universal Banks?
w: Narasimham-II (1998) recommended universal banking (and mergers of strong banks).

s: Which among the following do not fall under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949?
o: State Co-operative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (SCARDBs)
w: State Co-operative Agriculture & Rural Development Banks (land development banks) are outside the BR Act. SCBs, private banks and StCBs are covered.

s: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has ______ Local Boards in India
w: RBI has 4 Local Boards — North (New Delhi), South (Chennai), East (Kolkata), West (Mumbai).

s: Which of the following official is not a member of Central Board of RBI?
w: The Central Board: Governor, up to 4 Deputy Governors, 4 nominees from Local Boards, 10 government-nominated directors and 2 government officials. Executive Directors are not members.

s:
Which among the following is the correct sequence of establishment of Development Financial Institutions (DFIs)?
1. Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI)
2. Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM)
3. Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI)
4. Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
Which of the following Development Finance Institute is not established by RBI?
o: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation
w: EXIM Bank (1982) was set up by its own Act. NABARD, DICGC and IDBI have RBI origins.

s: Which among the following is the facility of EXIM Bank through which loans are provided to Sovereign Governments?
w: EXIM Bank extends Lines of Credit (LOCs) to foreign sovereign governments and their agencies so they can import from India. (Publisher key 'Project Exports' is wrong.)
r: EXIM to foreign governments = Lines of Credit.
note: Key corrected — publisher key D corrected to B (Lines of Credit)

s: Which among the following Development Financial Institutions is not a Specialised Financial Institutions?
w: EXIM, NABARD and TFCI are specialised financial institutions. UTI was an investment institution.

s: Which of the following facilities extended by SIDBI can be for a period of upto 10 years?
w: SMILE loans can be for up to 10 years (including moratorium up to 36 months).

s: Which of the following statement with respect to Self-Help Groups (SHGs) is incorrect?
o: Lending to SHGs constitute part of priority sector lending of banks.
Financing to SHGs by banks are refinanced upto an extent of 90% by NABARD
Advances to SHGs are included as part of lending to the weaker sections.
Loans to SHGs are provided collateral-free.
w: B is incorrect: NABARD refinances bank loans to SHGs up to 100%, not 90%. The other statements are correct.

s: Which among the following is not a kind of Micro Finance Institution (MFIs)?
w: MFIs are classified as not-for-profit, mutual benefit and for-profit (NBFC-MFIs). 'Green MFIs' is not a category.

s: As per the Reserve Bank of India (Regulatory Framework for Micro Finance Loans) Directions 2022, a micro finance loan is defined as a collateral-free loan given to a household, having annual household income up to______.
w: A microfinance loan is a collateral-free loan to a household with annual income up to ₹3 lakh.

s: Which among the following is NOT a correct feature of the 1997 amendments to Chapter III-B of the RBI Act?
o: Making it mandatory for NBFCs to obtain a Certificate of Registration (COR) from RBI.
Making it mandatory for NBFCs to maintain a minimum level of Net-Owned Funds (NOF).
Requiring all NBFCs to create a reserve fund and to transfer a sum, which is not less than 10% of their profits every year
Empowering RBI to file winding up petitions against NBFCs
w: The 1997 amendment requires the reserve fund transfer to be at least 20% (not 10%) of profits. CoR, minimum NOF and RBI's power to file winding-up petitions are genuine features.
note: Adapted PYQ — stem corrected to NOT-type (original key only fits that)

s: Which among the following entities regulates Chit Fund Companies?
w: Chit fund companies are regulated by the respective State Governments.

s: The regulatory minimum Net Owned Fund (NOF) for NBFC-ICC, NBFC-MFI and NBFC- Factors shall be increased to ______ as per the Scale-Based Regulation (SBR).
w: Under Scale-Based Regulation, minimum NOF for NBFC-ICC, NBFC-MFI and NBFC-Factors rises to ₹10 crore by 31 March 2027 (glide path).

s:
Consider the macroeconomic indicators given below:
1. GDP – $ 3.737 trillion
2. GVA - $ 2.787 trillion
3. Insurance Premium – $ 127 billion
4. Population – 141.1cr. Calculate the insurance density for the above given economy and mark the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
w: Insurance density = premium ÷ population = $127 bn ÷ 1.411 bn ≈ $90. (Penetration = premium ÷ GDP ≈ 3.4%.)
r: Density per head; penetration % of GDP.

s: Which of the following is not correct with reference to insurance brokers?
o: Insurance brokers are bound by Code of Conduct laid by IRDAI
Insurance brokers are not permitted to levy any fees for the advice
Insurance brokers can represent only one Insurance Company
Insurance brokers require to be licensed by IRDAI
w: C is not correct — brokers represent the CLIENT and can place business with many insurers. Agents are tied to one.

s: ______ is the limit of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in Insurance Intermediaries in India.
w: FDI in insurance intermediaries (brokers, TPAs, surveyors etc.) is 100% automatic (since 2019).

s: Which among the following cannot act as both borrowers and lenders in the Call, Notice & Term money market?
w: RRBs are not eligible participants in the call/notice/term money market; PDs, co-operative banks and SFBs are.

s: The applicant to become a Tri-Party Agent should have minimum paid-up equity share capital of ______.
w: A tri-party repo agent must have a minimum paid-up equity capital of ₹25 crore.

s: The minimum credit rating shall be ______ as per rating symbol for companies who can issue Commercial Papers?
w: Minimum credit rating for CP is A3.

s: The minimum amount that can be invested in a Certificate of deposit (CD) should be ______.
w: Minimum CD investment is ₹5 lakh.

s: ______ is an unsecured money market instrument issued in the form of a promissory note issued by private companies.
w: Commercial Paper is an unsecured money-market instrument in the form of a promissory note, issued by companies.

s: Individuals can participate in non-competitive basis as retail investors in auctions of Treasury Bills and the allocation in this case is restricted to a maximum of ______ within the notified amount.
w: Non-competitive bids in T-Bill auctions are capped at 5% of the notified amount.

s: Which among the following correctly defines Term Money?
o: Term money refers to borrowing/lending of funds for a period exceeding 14 days and upto one year on an uncollateralised basis
Term money refers to borrowing/lending of funds for a period exceeding 7 days and upto one year on an collateralised basis
Term money refers to borrowing/lending of funds for a period exceeding 7 days and upto one year on an uncollateralised basis
Term money refers to borrowing/lending of funds for a period exceeding 14 days and upto one year on a collateralised basis
w: Term money = borrowing/lending for more than 14 days and up to one year, uncollateralised.
note: Adapted PYQ — stem corrected (original "incorrect" did not match the key)

s: Notice money means borrowing or lending in ______
o: Notice money refers to borrowing/lending of funds for a period exceeding 7 days and upto one year on an uncollateralised basis
Notice money refers to borrowing/lending of funds for a period exceeding 2 days and upto 14 days on an collateralised basis
Notice money refers to borrowing/lending of funds for a period exceeding 2 days and upto 14 days on an uncollateralised basis
Notice money refers to borrowing/lending of funds for a period exceeding 14 days and upto one year on a collateralised basis
w: Notice money = more than 1 day (2 days) up to 14 days, uncollateralised.

s: Which among the following is the Reserve Bank of India's Core Banking Solution system?
w: e-Kuber is RBI's Core Banking Solution (also its auction platform).

s:
Which among following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. India is one of the fastest growing economies but is one of the most unequal societies.
2. As per World Inequality Report 2022, the poorest half of the global population “barely owns any wealth” possessing just 2% of the total wealth.
3. The causes of migration are linked through environment to political, economic and societal causes and thus distinguishing pure environment induced causes of migration is easy.
4. Jobless growth is a situation wherein the level of unemployment either remain stagnant or decreases.
w: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: because environmental causes are tied up with political, economic and social ones, isolating purely environment-induced migration is DIFFICULT, not easy.
r: Jobless growth = output grows, employment doesn't.

s: A company shall be eligible to issue Commercial Paper provided the tangible net worth of the company, as per the latest audited balance sheet, is not less than ______.
w: A company may issue CP if its tangible net worth is at least ₹4 crore.

s: Which among the following statement is correct with respect to a Red Herring Prospectus?
o: An offer document for the purpose of Qualified Institutional Placement
An offer document that must state the final issue price
It provides detailed information about the company's business operations, financials, promoters and objects of the issue
w: An RHP gives detailed information on the company's business, financials, promoters and objects of the issue (but no final price).
note: Adapted PYQ — option B reworded (original B was also correct)

s: Which among the following is the correct description of V-shaped recovery in an economy?
o: It is a quick, sharp improvement in an economy after a sharp decline.
It is an unusual scenario where certain industries and individuals pull out of a recession, while others stagnate.
It is a type of recovery characterized by a slow rate of recovery, with persistent unemployment and stagnant economic growth
It is the most-optimistic scenario in which the economy quickly rises after an economic crash.
w: A V-shaped recovery is a quick, sharp improvement after a sharp decline. B describes a K-shaped recovery; C describes an L-/U-shaped slow recovery.

s: The Prudential Limit for Primary Dealers for transacting as part of Call and Notice Money market is ______.
o: 100% of capital funds, on a daily average basis in a reporting fortnight
125% of capital funds on any given day
225% of Net Owned Fund (NoF) as at the end of the previous financial year on a daily average basis in a reporting fortnight.
225% of Net Owned Fund (NoF) as at the end of the previous financial year.
w: PDs may borrow in call/notice money up to 225% of NOF at the end of the previous year (daily average in a fortnight).

s: Transaction permitted in Central Govt securities that have been notified but not yet actually issued are known as “When Issued”. In this context, identify the correct statement
o: NRIs are eligible to undertake only Long position
NRIs are eligible to undertake only Short position
OCIs can undertake both Long & Short positions
HUFs can undertake both Long & Short positions
w: In 'When Issued' trading, non-residents (NRIs) may take only long (buy) positions, as keyed.

s:
Consider that a person has bought Government Securities in India on 23rd December
2022. What is the date of settlement?
w: G-secs settle T+1 working day: bought Friday 23 Dec 2022 → settles Monday 26 Dec 2022. (The publisher's '24 Dec', a Saturday, is wrong.)
note: Key corrected — publisher key B corrected to D — T+1 working day

s: Which among the following is an instrument used by companies to raise funds to supply long-term investment products, for long-term investors?
w: Corporate bonds are issued by companies to raise long-term funds from long-term investors.

s:
Which among the following is one of the participant(s) of Forex Market?
1. RBI
2. Authorised Dealers
3. Customers
4. SEBI
w: As keyed, forex participants include RBI (intervention), authorised dealers and customers. The book also lists SEBI as a market-related regulator.

s: Which among the following is the enforcement authority of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999?
o: Foreign Exchange Department, State Bank of India.
Directorate of Enforcement, Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
Capital Market Division, Ministry of Commerce
w: The Directorate of Enforcement (Department of Revenue, MoF) enforces FEMA.

s: Appeals against the decisions of the Adjudicating Authorities and Special Director (Appeals) are heard by which among the following?
w: Under FEMA, appeals against Adjudicating Authorities and the Special Director (Appeals) go to the Appellate Tribunal. (Publisher key 'Competent Authority' is wrong.)
note: Key corrected — publisher key D corrected to C — Appellate Tribunal

s: In the foreign exchange market, settlement of a SPOT transaction takes place:
o: On one day after the Trading day
On one month after the Trading day
On two days after the Trading day
w: Forex spot deals settle two working days after the trade date (T+2). Same-day is 'cash/ready'; next day is 'tom'. (Publisher key 'same day' is wrong.)
r: Cash T+0 · Tom T+1 · Spot T+2.
note: Key corrected — publisher key A corrected to D — spot = T+2

s: Which among the following is the Alternate Reference Rate of USA suggested to be used by various central Banks in substitution of LIBOR?
w: The US ARR is SOFR (Secured Overnight Financing Rate).

s: Which of the following is not one of the 6 currencies in the US Dollar Index?
w: USDX basket: euro, yen, pound, Canadian dollar, Swedish krona and Swiss franc. The Chinese yuan is not included.

s: In the context of interconnectedness of Capital market which among the following statements is correct?
o: Bond Market & Money Market move in tandem
Equity markets normally move negatively in relation to bond yields
Equity markets and bond yields move in random ways
w: Equity prices normally move inversely to bond yields (higher yields → lower equity valuations).

s: In respect of every issue to be managed by the lead merchant banker holding a certificate under Category-I shall accept a minimum underwriting obligation of ______ of the total underwriting commitment or Rs 25 lacs, whichever is less
w: The lead merchant banker (Category I) must underwrite at least 5% of the total underwriting commitment or ₹25 lakh, whichever is less.

s: All OTC trades in CDs shall be reported within ______ of the trade on the reporting platform of Clearcorp Dealing Systems (India) Ltd. (CDSIL)
w: OTC trades in CDs must be reported within 15 minutes on CCIL's F-TRAC platform.

s: Which of the following statement is true regarding Certificate of Deposits?
o: It is issued at Discounted Value & redeemed at par value
It is issued at par value & redeemed at discounted values
It is issued at par value & redeemed at premium value
It is issued at par value & redeemed at the same value
w: CDs are issued at a discount and redeemed at par.

s: Which of the following statement is incorrect regarding call & put option?
o: A call option is a right to buy an underlying asset at a fixed price at a future date.
A put option is the right to sell an underlying asset at a fixed price at a future date.
A call option is the obligation of the option writer to sell an underlying asset at a fixed price at a future date.
A put option is the obligation of the option buyer to buy an underlying asset at a fixed price at a future date.
w: D is incorrect: a put gives its BUYER the right to SELL; the put WRITER has the obligation to buy.

s: Which among the following statement is not correct with respect to Derivatives?
o: Forward Agreements are traded Over the Counter.
Swaps deal with exchange of financial flows.
w: Forwards are OTC with flexible maturities; swaps exchange cash flows. Treating futures as 'negotiable instruments' is the incorrect statement, as keyed.

s: Which among the following statement is correct with respect to Derivatives?
o: Futures require no margins for trading
w: As per the book, forwards (OTC) can be traded 24×7. Futures have fixed maturities, standard amounts and require margins.

s: If a corporate has to borrow, for a period of 3 months, 6 months from now, it is referred to as a ______ FRA.
w: Borrowing for 3 months starting 6 months from now = 6 × 9 FRA.

s: Which among the following statement is correct with respect to the
o: The transactions processed under TReDS are without recourse to the MSMEs
The transactions processed under TReDS are with recourse to the MSMEs
The transactions processed under TReDS are both with recourse and without recourse to the MSMEs
w: TReDS transactions are without recourse to the MSME seller.

s: Which among the following statement is correct with respect to Bill Discounting and Factoring?
o: Bill Discounting is always without recourse
Bill Discounting involves assignment of debt
w: Factoring involves assignment of debts (receivables) to the factor; bill discounting does not, and is usually with recourse.

s: Venture Capital investments are generally ______opportunities
w: Venture capital investments are high-risk, high-return.

s:
Match the credit rating symbols with their description:
A. AA
B. BBB
C. B
D. C

i. Vulnerable to default
ii. High risk
iii. High safety
iv. Moderate safety
w: Rating meanings: AA = high safety; BBB = moderate safety; B = high risk; C = very high risk / vulnerable to default.
r: AAA highest · AA high · A adequate · BBB moderate · BB moderate risk · B high risk · C very high risk · D default.

s: The classification of Mutual Funds into open-ended and close-ended schemes is done based on which among the following criteria?
w: Open-ended vs close-ended is a classification by maturity/structure (redemption at any time vs fixed tenure).

s: Net Asset Value (NAV ) for Index/Debt Mutual Fund & NAV for Equity Mutual Funds have to be rounded off to ______ & ______ places.
w: NAV is computed to 4 decimals for debt/index funds and 2 decimals for equity funds, as keyed.

s: Which among the following was established by the Indian Government to develop the Mutual Funds sector in India?
w: UTI was established by the Government (1963) to develop the mutual fund sector.

s:
Which among the following is the correct match? Category of Mutual Fund MF Characteristic
1. Index Fund i. Lock in 3 years
2. Liquid Fund ii. 95% investment in underlying funds
3. Equity Linked Savings Scheme iii. 95% investment in Particular Index (ELSS)
4. Fund of Fund iv. Debt & Money Market Securities with maturity upto 91 days
w: Index fund — 95% in the index; liquid fund — debt/money market up to 91 days; ELSS — 3-year lock-in; fund of funds — 95% in underlying funds.

s: Risk-o-meter- risk levels are categorised into ______ levels.
w: SEBI's risk-o-meter has six levels: Low, Low-to-Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High and Very High.

s: The life cover under the Prime Minister Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) is ______.
w: PMJJBY life cover is ₹2 lakh.

s: The PMJJBY is available to people in the age group of ______years
w: PMJJBY entry age is 18–50 years.

s: The risk coverage under the Prime Minister Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) is ______ for accidental death and full disability.
w: PMSBY cover is ₹2 lakh for accidental death or full disability.

s: As part of the Employees Provident Fund Scheme, the employer's matching contributions are allocated across EPF and EPS such that ______goes into the EPF, the remaining ______ goes into the EPS.
w: Of the employer's 12% contribution, 8.33% goes to the EPS (pension) and 3.67% to the EPF.

s: UAN is generated and allotted by the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). It is a unique______ digit number.
w: UAN is a 12-digit number allotted by EPFO.

s: Under the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) the minimum guaranteed pension of ______ per month is provided after the subscriber attains the age of 60 years.
w: APY guarantees a monthly pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 from age 60.

s: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is being carried out by ______.
w: APY is administered by PFRDA through the NPS architecture.

s: Which of the following is not a type of REIT?
w: As keyed, the IIBF book lists residential, healthcare and office REITs; 'industrial' is treated as the odd one out.

s: Not less than ______of net distributable cash flow of the Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) are to be distributed to unit holders.
w: REITs (and InvITs) must distribute at least 90% of net distributable cash flows to unit holders.

s: The percentage of interest subsidy provided under the Interest Subsidy Eligibility Certificate (ISEC) is ______.
w: Under the ISEC scheme the interest subsidy is 4% (as keyed in the IIBF book).

s: Which among the following international organisations have been supporting the Swachh Bharat Mission and National Rural Livelihoods Project in India?
w: The World Bank has supported the Swachh Bharat Mission and the National Rural Livelihoods Project.

s: Under category of Social Infrastructure, loans up to a limit of ₹______ per borrower for building health care facilities under ‘Ayushman Bharat’ in Tier II to Tier VI centres are eligible for priority sector classification.
w: Loans up to ₹10 crore per borrower for building healthcare facilities under Ayushman Bharat in Tier II–VI centres qualify as social infrastructure PSL.

s: As per the latest regulations of RBI, all banks are required to exchange Rs 2000 bank notes up to a maximum of ______ at a time starting from May 23, 2023.
w: RBI allowed exchange of ₹2000 notes up to ₹20,000 at a time from 23 May 2023.

s:
Which among the following is one of the component(s) of the Green Development Framework of RBI?
1. Energy efficiency
2. Pollution
3. Health infrastructure
4. Enhancing natural ecosystems and biodiversity
w: RBI's green framework components include energy efficiency, pollution prevention/control and protection of natural ecosystems & biodiversity. Health infrastructure is social, not green.

s: The term Hindu Rate of Growth was coined by ______.
w: Prof. Raj Krishna coined 'Hindu rate of growth' (1978) for India's ~3.5% growth between the 1950s and 1980s.
r: Hindu rate of growth = Raj Krishna, ~3.5%.

s: Which among the following statement is incorrect with respect to different sectors of the Indian Economy in relation to the COVID pandemic?
o: The recovery has been uneven among services, with financial, real estate, and professional services, as well as public administration, defence, and other services, gaining traction and exceeding their respective pre-pandemic levels.
Recovery in the trade, hotel, transportation, communication, and broadcasting-related sectors, has exceeded pre-pandemic levels.
Different sectors of the economy are recovering to varying degrees
Agriculture survived the pandemic's multiple waves, industry and construction are on the rebound
w: Statement B is incorrect: recovery in trade, hotels, transport, communication and broadcasting was gradual and had NOT exceeded pre-pandemic levels. Financial/real-estate/professional services and public administration did recover beyond pre-pandemic levels.

s: Which among the following is the correct definition of 'Sunrise Sector'?
o: It is the sector which includes all those activities the end purpose of which consists in exploiting natural resources
It is the sector that covers all those activities consisting in varying degrees of processing of raw materials.
It includes all those activities in which an industry that has existed for a long time and that is less successful and making less profit than previously
It is one that is still in its infancy but has the potential for significant growth.
w: A sunrise sector is still in its infancy but has potential for significant growth. A = primary sector, B = secondary sector, C = sunset sector.

s: As per the latest definition of MSMEs of the Indian Government, for a Small Enterprise, the investment in plant and machinery should not exceed Rs.______ and turnover should not exceed Rs.______
w: Revised MSME criteria (from 1 Apr 2025): Small = investment ≤ ₹25 crore and turnover ≤ ₹100 crore. The old ₹10 cr/₹50 cr limits are outdated.
note: Adapted PYQ — updated to 2025 MSME limits

s: Individual Micro and Small Enterprises can apply for collateral-free loans up to ______ from the Ministry of MSME and SIDBI under the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro & Small Enterprises (CGTMSE).
w: CGTMSE guarantee cover for micro and small enterprises was raised to ₹10 crore (from ₹5 crore) with effect from 1 April 2025. The old answer of ₹1 crore is outdated.
note: Adapted PYQ — answer updated: CGTMSE cover ₹10 crore from April 2025

s: Which among the following is an example of Soft Infrastructure?
w: Law-enforcement organisations are soft infrastructure; ports, airports and pipelines are hard infrastructure.

s:
Which among the following is/are the characteristic feature(s) of Foreign Institutional Investments?
1. It has long-term perspective.
2. It is generally volatile in nature.
3. It goes into Hedge Funds.
w: FII is volatile and goes into hedge funds, but has a SHORT-term perspective, so 2 and 3.

s:
Which among the following is/are the function(s) of International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
1. Surveillance over members' economic policies
2. Combating poverty in low-income countries
3. Strengthening the International Monetary System
4. Increasing the global supply of international reserves
w: IMF functions: surveillance, lending including concessional lending to fight poverty in low-income members, strengthening the monetary system, and adding to global reserves via SDRs — all four.

s: In India, companies are now free to spend more than the mandated ______ per cent of their net profits on Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) in any year.
w: CSR minimum is 2% of average net profit; companies may spend more and carry forward the excess (up to 3 years).

s: As per the latest amendment in the Companies Act 2013, non-compliance with Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) provisions is______.
w: After the 2021 amendment, CSR non-compliance was decriminalised into a civil wrong attracting monetary penalty (no imprisonment).
r: CSR breach = civil penalty, not jail.

s: Who among the following pioneered the principle of 'conspicuous consumption'?
w: Thorstein Veblen coined 'conspicuous consumption' (Theory of the Leisure Class, 1899).

s:
Consider the following:
1. Net bank credit to the government.
2. Bank credit to the commercial sector.
3. Net foreign exchange assets of the banking sector.
4. Government's currency liabilities to the public.
5. Net non-monetary liabilities of the banking sector. Which among the following is correct with respect to the sources of Money Supply (M3) in Indian economy?
o: Sources of Money Supply (M3) in Indian economy = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5
Sources of Money Supply (M3) in Indian economy = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 - 5
Sources of Money Supply (M3) in Indian economy = 1 + 2 - 3 + 4 + 5
Sources of Money Supply (M3) in Indian economy = 1 - 2 - 3 - 4 - 5
w: Sources of M3 = Net bank credit to government + bank credit to commercial sector + net foreign exchange assets of the banking sector + government currency liabilities to the public − net non-monetary liabilities of the banking sector.

s: The Liquidity Preference Theory of Interest was propounded by ______.
w: Liquidity preference theory was propounded by J.M. Keynes.

s:
Which among the following is/are the characteristic(s) of the Boom of Business Cycle?
1. An accelerated and prolonged increase in demand
2. Demand peaks to levels that exceed sustainable output/production levels
3. Economy heats up and a demand-supply lag becomes apparent
w: In a boom demand rises fast and stays high, exceeds sustainable output, and the economy overheats with demand-supply lags — all three.

s:
The Rate of Interest as per Liquidity Preference Theory is determined by which among the following?
1. Demand for money
2. Supply of money
3. Rate of savings
w: Under liquidity preference, interest is fixed by the demand for money and the supply of money. Savings determine interest in the classical theory.

s:
Which among the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. The Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) corridor at present is determined by the MSF as the upper band
2. Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) is the lower band of LAF
3. Repo rate is the centre of the LAF corridor.
w: The LAF corridor: MSF = upper band, SDF = lower band, repo = centre. All three are correct.

s: The funds availed by banks under Targeted Long-Term Repo Operations (TLTRO) 2.0 was supposed to be invested in investment grade bonds, commercial paper, and non-convertible debentures of NBECs, with at least ______of the total amount availed going to small and mid-sized NBFCs and MFIs.
w: Under TLTRO 2.0 at least 50% of the funds availed had to go to small and mid-sized NBFCs and MFIs.

s: Gross Domestic Product in India is mainly calculated using ______ method.
o: A mix of all the three
w: As keyed in the IIBF book, India's GDP (headline, by demand side) is primarily estimated using the expenditure method. NSO actually compiles the production (value-added) side as the primary estimate, so treat this as a book-specific answer.

s: Which among the following bank was not nationalised in 1969 in India?
w: Andhra Bank was nationalised in 1980. Allahabad Bank, Bank of Maharashtra and Bank of Baroda were among the 14 nationalised in 1969.

s:
Which among the following is/are the recommendations of the Narasimham Committee - I (1991)?
1. Establishment of a 4-tier hierarchy for banking structure.
2. A phased reduction in Statutory Liquidity Ratio.
3. Phased achievement of 10% Capital Adequacy Ratio.
w: Narasimham-I proposed a 4-tier banking structure and phased SLR reduction; CRAR target was 8%, not 10%. So 1 and 2.

s: Whatsapp pay is a
w: WhatsApp Pay is a techfin company.

s: As per Section 4 of the RBI Act, the paid-up capital of the Bank shall be ______.
w: Sec 4 RBI Act: paid-up capital ₹5 crore.

s: As per Section 13 of the RBI Act, Meetings of the Central Board shall be convened by the Governor at least ______times in each year.
w: Sec 13 RBI Act: the Central Board meets at least six times a year and at least once each quarter.

s: The Minimum loan size for Equipment Finance under the SIDBI Make in India Soft Loan Fund for MSMEs (SIDBI SMILE) is ______.
w: Minimum loan size under SMILE for equipment finance is ₹10 lakh.

s:
Which among the following is/are the function(s) of EXIM Bank of India?
1. Financing the import and export of goods and services from countries other than India.
2. Financing the import or export of machines and machinery on lease or hire purchase basis.
3. Providing refinancing services to banks and other financial institutions for their financing of foreign trade.
4. Underwriting shares/debentures of companies, engaged in foreign trade.
w: All four are EXIM Bank functions, including underwriting shares/debentures of foreign-trade companies.

s: An Asset Finance Company in India is one whose income arising out of the principal business is not less than ______ of its total assets and total income.
w: An Asset Finance Company has financing of real/physical assets for productive activity of at least 60% of total assets and income from it of at least 60% of total income.

s:
Which among the following statement(s) is/are correct with respect to National Asset Reconstruction Bank (NARCL) and India Debt Resolution Co. Ltd (IDRCL)?
1. NARCL has been set up by banks to aggregate and consolidate stressed assets for their subsequent resolution
2. IDRCL is a service company/operational entity which will manage the asset and engage market professionals and turnaround experts.
3. For NARCL, public sector banks will hold 51% of the equity capital.
4. In the case of IDRCL, public sector banks will hold 49% of the capital
w: All four are correct: NARCL is set up by banks; IDRCL is the operating/service company; PSBs hold 51% of NARCL and up to 49% of IDRCL.

s:
Price Discovery in the financial markets is affected by which among the following?
1. Supply and demand
2. Attitudes to risk
3. Volatility
4. Available information
5. Market mechanisms
w: Price discovery depends on supply and demand, risk attitudes, volatility, information and market mechanisms — all five.

s: The Prudential Limit for Scheduled Commercial Banks for transacting as part of Call and Notice Money market is ______ % of capital funds on a daily average basis in a reporting fortnight.
w: SCBs' call/notice borrowing limit is 100% of capital funds (daily average in a fortnight; up to 125% on any day). Lending limit is 50% of capital funds.

s:
Which among the statement(s) given below is/are correct?
1. A Reverse repo transaction involves the buying of securities and lending of short-term surplus in the 1st leg and selling the security at a predetermined rate in the 2nd leg.
2. Seller promises to repurchase in a Repo transaction.
3. The seller of the security receives funds, while the buyer of the security receives collateral for the funds that has been lent in a Repo transaction.
4. Repo is a repurchase agreement, entered into between eligible counterparties for borrowing and lending of funds, on a collateralised basis.
w: All four statements correctly describe repo/reverse repo: seller repurchases, funds vs collateral, and collateralised borrowing between eligible counterparties.

s:
Which among the following is/are the services provided by the intermediary in a Tri-party Repo Contract?
1. Collateral selection
2. Payment and settlement
3. Custody and management
w: A tri-party intermediary handles collateral selection, payment & settlement and custody/management — all three.

s: The tenors of the term repos conducted by the RBI under Long Term Repo Operations (LTRO) were between ______.
w: RBI's LTROs (2020) were of 1-year and 3-year tenors.

s:
Which among the following is/are the prime objective(s) of Targeted Long Term Repo Operations (TLTRO) of RBI?
1. Providing liquidity to the corporate bond market.
2. Supporting the merchants.
3. Supporting MSME sector.
w: TLTRO's prime objective was to supply liquidity to the corporate bond/CP/NCD market.

s:
Which among the following instrument(s) is/are traded in the Secondary Markets?
1. Equity
2. Equity Shares
3. Rights Issue
4. Bonus Shares
w: Equity, equity shares and shares from rights/bonus issues all trade in the secondary market once listed.

s: Consider that a person has bought shares of Reliance on 23rd December 2022. What is the date of settlement?
w: Equity settles T+1 working day: bought Friday 23 Dec 2022 → settles Monday 26 Dec 2022. (The publisher's '24 Dec' is a Saturday — wrong.)
note: Key corrected — publisher key B (a Saturday) corrected to D — T+1 working day

s: State Development Loans are generally issued by auction, which is carried out by the Reserve Bank of India and pay ______ interest at the coupon rate.
w: SDLs pay coupon half-yearly.

s:
Which among the following Securitie(s) is/are eligible under the RBI Retail Direct Scheme?
1. Government of India Treasury Bills
2. Government of India dated securities
3. Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGB)
4. AAA rate Corporate Bonds.
w: Under RDS individuals can buy T-Bills, dated G-secs, SDLs and SGBs. Corporate bonds are not offered.

s: Which of the following bond theorems is not correct?
o: The price of a bond is inversely related to the change in interest rate.
The increase in the price of a bond when the interest rate goes down by a certain percentage, is greater than the decrease in its price when the interest rate goes up by the same percentage.
Longer the term to maturity of a bond, lower will be its price sensitivity.
Between two bonds of same maturity but different coupons, the bond with the lower coupon will experience more price sensitivity than the one with higher coupon.
w: C is wrong: the LONGER the maturity, the HIGHER the price sensitivity. The other three are correct bond theorems.

s:
Which among the following is/are the member bank(s) of Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India (FEDAI)?
1. Brokers
2. Public Sector Bank
3. Private Sector Bank
4. Foreign Sector Bank
w: FEDAI members are banks (public, private, foreign) authorised to deal in forex. Brokers are only accredited, not members.

s:
Which among the following is/are the function(s) of the Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India (FEDAI)?
1. Training of bank personnel in the areas of foreign exchange
2. Accreditation of forex brokers
3. Announcement of daily and periodical rates to member banks.
w: FEDAI trains bank staff, accredits brokers and announces daily/periodical rates to members — all three.

s: Which among the following country is not a member of Asian Clearing Union (ACU)?
w: Afghanistan is not an ACU member. Members: India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Iran, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka.

s: As per the SEBI Regulations on Merchant Banking, a Merchant Bank that can act as underwriter, advisor, consultant to an issue is ______.
w: Category III merchant bankers can act as underwriter, adviser and consultant. Category I can do everything including issue management; Category II as co-manager, adviser, consultant, underwriter; Category IV only adviser/consultant.

s:
As per the Key Policy Requirements for Merchant Banks as per SEBI Regulations, which among the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. Annually audited result should be submitted to SEBI.
2. Lead Merchant Bank should not associate with a merchant banker, without registration Merchant Bank should not act as such for an associate.
3. Every merchant bank shall appoint a Compliance Officer to monitor compliance with prevailing Regulations.
w: Merchant bankers must not associate with unregistered merchant bankers and must appoint a compliance officer. Statement 1 is not one of the listed key requirements (as keyed). So 2 and 3.

s: Which among the following statement is incorrect with respect to a Derivative?
o: It is a financial instrument whose value changes in response to the change in the underlying entity.
It is a financial instrument that requires high initial net investment
It is a financial instrument that is settled at a future date.
w: Derivatives need little or no initial net investment, so B is incorrect.

s: Which among the following statement is incorrect with respect to the Forward contracts?
o: Forward contracts are traded Over the Counter
Forward contracts have counterparty in direct contact
w: A is incorrect: forwards have FLEXIBLE (customised) maturities.

s: In which among the following kind of International Factoring, the import factor comes into focus only if the buyer defaults in making the payment?
w: In the single factor system the import factor comes in only if the buyer defaults.

s:
Which among the following entities are the participants in Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS)?
1. MSME sellers
2. Corporate buyers
3. Government Departments
4. Public Sector Undertakings
5. NBFC factors
w: TReDS participants: MSME sellers, corporate buyers, government departments, PSUs and financiers including NBFC-factors — all five.

s:
Which among the following is/are not the feature(s) of Venture Capital Finance?
1. They are high risk investments made with an intention of making high profits.
2. Investments are generally done in innovative projects.
3. The investments are made in brown field entities.
4. The provider of venture capital can participate in the management of the company.
w: VC is high-risk, invests in innovative projects and allows management participation. It invests in new (greenfield/start-up) ventures, not brownfield entities, so 3 is not a feature.

s:
Which among the following is/are the exit routes for Venture Capital Finance?
1. Buy back of Shares by the Promoters
2. Liquidation of the Investee Company
3. Initial Public Offering
w: VC exits: promoter buy-back, IPO, sale to strategic buyer, or (in failure) liquidation — all three listed.

s: An airline owner wants to use an aircraft on lease. Which among the following is the most appropriate kind of leasing?
w: An airline using an aircraft for a period without ownership intent typically takes an operating lease.

s: Which among the following is the effect of leasing on debt-equity ratio due to leasing an asset?
w: As per the book, leasing does not change the debt-equity ratio (no borrowing appears on the balance sheet).

s:
Which among the following is not a feature of Hire Purchase?
1. Hire purchaser does not become the owner of the asset even after paying the last instalment.
2. Only the interest element included in the hire-purchase instalments are in nature of revenue expenditure.
3. Hire purchaser cannot claim for depreciation.
4. Hire purchaser can claim interest payment from the taxable income.
w: Not HP features: 1 (the hirer DOES become owner after the last instalment) and 3 (the hirer CAN claim depreciation). Statements 2 and 4 are true.

s: Credit Rating Agencies in India classify ratings into ______ grades?
w: As keyed, CRAs group ratings into three broad grades: investment grade, speculative grade and default.

s: A ______ fund is an open-ended debt scheme investing in government securities across maturity.
w: A gilt fund is an open-ended debt scheme investing at least 80% in G-secs across maturities.

s: Mr. Rajesh owns a restaurant, which he bought three year ago, for Rs. 50 lakhs. He had bought fire insurance worth Rs. 40 lakhs. His restaurant caught fire and he suffered a loss of Rs. 50 lakhs. The amount of compensation to be paid by the insurance company is ______.
w: Under-insurance attracts the average clause: claim = loss × (sum insured ÷ value) = 50 × 40/50 = ₹40 lakh. Here it equals the sum insured.

s: The risk coverage under the Prime Minister Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) is for ______ in case of death of the insured, due to any reason.
w: PMJJBY pays ₹2 lakh on death from any cause.

s: The lock-in period for the Public Provident Fund (PPF) Scheme is ______ years.
w: PPF lock-in period is 15 years.

s: An Indian citizen resident in London wants to join Atal Pension Yojana. Which among the following statement is correct in this regard?
o: He can join if his age is greater than 40 years.
One of the eligibility conditions is that he has a valid savings bank account/post office savings account.
He can join only after taking permission from EPFO.
He can join only after taking permission from SEBI and RBI.
w: APY needs a savings bank or post office savings account (and entry age 18–40).

s: Pick the odd one out of the following
